On day 9 of therapy, he reported loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice.
He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily.

decisive_items: He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily.
On day 9 of therapy, he reported loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice.
Serologic tests for HBsAg, anti-HBc IgM, anti-HCV, anti-HAV IgM, anti-HEV, HEV RNA, and HCV RNA were negative.
response.rationale: R2 is the most specific supported diagnosis: hepatocellular injury began 9 days after Alfuzosin was started and other causes were excluded; R4 is only the injury pattern, and R3 is not supported because ALP is normal and MRCP shows normal biliary anatomy.

rejected.why: Describes the acute hepatocellular pattern but does not include the drug/temporal and exclusion evidence that makes R2 the diagnosis.
Cholestatic jaundice is not supported: ALP is normal, GGT is only mildly elevated, and MRCP shows normal biliary anatomy.
